diagnosis: First playbook, written from the lessons of stages E-P, D and M and the operator's notes (too pessimistic, priced-in as a claim to prove, creative sources as one workflow, freshest data). Also frozen as control.md.

hp.v1 has 35 resolved names over 3 run days (11-06, 11-09, 11-10). Brier is 0.2492, a skill of 0.003 over a coin. Direction is 16/32 and there are 0 recommendations. The control (also hp.v1, frozen) has 12 names at Brier 0.2416. The paired difference on those 12 is -0.004 (sd 0.031, t -0.45), and because both arms ran the same text, that figure is the stage's reproducibility noise, not an effect. The views carry no information yet, and the reason is not miscalibration: every evolving p_up sits between 38 and 58, and only 3 of 35 are 10 or more points from 50. That spread is honest for a researcher with no edge. Two mechanisms in the playbook keep it there. (1) The researchers read P7's mechanism clause together with P4 and P8 as 'the deciding line must be visible before the release'. It never is, so on name after name they gathered dated evidence on the inputs to that line and then sat near 50 with 'no public trace before the release' (QBTS, HSAI, CRWV, RKLB, STUB, HIMS, LQDA). Where the inputs pointed, the facts often followed. RKLB's guide-beat record was right: record revenue, backlog +52% q/q, Q4 guided to record revenue and margin expansion. CRWV's counterparty capacity was on time and the stock rose 14.9%. The recommendation channel produced nothing in 47 views, so it cannot even be evaluated. (2) Five researchers wrote, without prompting, that taking the run-in apart against peers and the tape was their most useful step and that the playbook does not name it (HSAI, QBTS, RKLB, TTD, LPTH). Separately, P6's positioning sentence is wrong as written: it says a crowded short makes a good print move less. Researchers instead pulled p_up toward 50 for squeeze risk (ASTS, LPTH, FRNM); direction against crowded shorts was 3 of 6, which says positioning is size, not sign. Stage E-P's selected calls on the same names went 5 of 6 (+8.2%, t 1.91), and its sign over all 34 names with a move was 21 of 34. Stage H agreed in sign on all 6 selected names but stayed at 38-58, so the evidence was not missing; the playbook would not let it count. Nothing here rests on returns. The 11-06 day ran without hunt files, so it is cited nowhere. The run-in names that fell (QBTS, HSAI, RKLB, TTD, LPTH, ASTS) mostly exited on one market morning, so they are correlated, and no direction rule is drawn from them.

ops.title: How the reaction is decided
ops.text:
A stock trades on the line it trades on: often the guide, the one segment, the one metric the last reactions turned on, not the headline EPS. Find that line first. Read the last reactions and what caused them.

Then take the run-in apart before you read it. Over the last five to twenty sessions, set this stock's move beside its closest peers, its sector basket and the index, and ask which part came with this company's own news and which came with peers' prints or the tape. A move that came with a peer's results or with the market is not evidence about this company. It shifts the bar this release has to clear without saying whether the release clears it. So ask whether this company's own evidence supports the level the peers or the tape took it to. Where it does not, the price is ahead of the evidence, which is as real a gap as a stale estimate; where it does, the move is not a reason to fade it. For a high-beta name, say how large an ordinary overnight or morning move is on market noise alone, and keep p_up about what the release does to the price, not about the tape.

Positioning sets the size more than the direction: a crowded short makes a good print move more and a bad one less; a big run-up makes a good print move less and a bad one more. Put a possible squeeze into `abs_move_pct`, not into a pull toward 50. Remember the window you are scored on (your definition states it): a reaction that needs weeks to play out does not count.
ops.rationale: The researchers kept inventing the same step (peer and tape decomposition of the run-in) and naming its absence as a gap. Putting it in the playbook makes it routine, and makes it say what the decomposition means for p_up: a peer- or tape-driven level is a bar raised without this company's evidence, which is a positioning fact, not a direction. The old positioning sentence was garbled: it lumped a crowded short with a big run-up, and the researchers worked around it by pulling p_up toward 50 for squeeze risk. Positioning direction was 3 of 6 against crowded shorts (ASTS, LPTH, TTD down; CRWV, CAPR, FRNM up), which fits 'size, not sign'. The edit does not prescribe fading rallies. The six run-in names that fell mostly exited on one market morning and are not used as evidence of direction.
ops.predicted_effect: In hp.v2 hunts whose sealed 5-day or 20-day run-up is 8% or more in absolute size, at least 80% carry in `market_holds` an explicit split of the run-in into own news, peers and tape. approach_notes stop naming the decomposition as missing (it was named in 5 of 31 resolved hunt files under hp.v1). questions_pursued no longer record moves toward 50 justified only by squeeze risk. On paired names, hp.v2's Brier is no worse than the control's.
ops.revert_if: Two outcomes would show this was wrong. First, over at least 30 resolved hp.v2 names, the names whose hunt attributes most of the run-in to peers or the tape score a worse paired Brier than the control on the same names (mean difference above +0.01). Second, the decomposition is absent from most qualifying hunts, so the text changed nothing and should be removed.

ops.title: Calibration and when to recommend
ops.text:
`p_up` is your honest probability that the stock is higher at the end of the window. 50 means you cannot tell. Move away from 50 only as far as the evidence takes you.

The line a print turns on (the next-period guide, the margin, bookings) is almost never visible before the release. That is the normal case and not, by itself, a reason to stay at 50. What you can see are its inputs: the company's record of guiding against what it then reported, counterparties' and peers' disclosures since it last spoke, your own arithmetic of what the line needs, and what consensus and the price assume about it. Estimate which way the line is likely to land against what the price holds, and let that estimate set p_up. Not being able to see the line is not the same as having shown that the price holds it (P8).

Recommend (`action` long or short) only when all three hold:
- your probability that the direction is right is 65 or more;
- you can name the mechanism: the dated evidence that makes one side of the deciding line more likely than the price assumes, the reason the price does not hold it, and why this release will show it inside the window;
- your strongest case against it (`self_critique`) does not change your mind.

There is no quota. Zero recommendations on a day is fine; so are several.
ops.rationale: As read by the researchers, the old mechanism clause asked for the release's content to be seen before the release, a condition no print can meet. On seven resolved names the researcher found dated evidence on the inputs to the deciding line and then explicitly declined to let it move p_up because the line itself 'has no public trace before the release' (QBTS, HSAI, CRWV, RKLB, STUB, HIMS, LQDA). After the fact the inputs were often right on the facts: RKLB beat and guided up with margin expansion, as its guiding record suggested, and CRWV's counterparty capacity was on time before the stock rose 14.9%. The result was 0 recommendations in 47 views and only 3 of 35 p_up values 10 or more points from 50. The edit keeps the 65 bar and the three conditions, and changes only what the mechanism must show: evidence that one side of the line is more likely than the price assumes, not sight of the line. It rests on the reasoning failure, not on returns.
ops.predicted_effect: p_up spreads out: the share of hp.v2 views with |p_up - 50| of 10 or more rises from 3/35 (9%) to at least 20%. At least 3 recommendations appear over the first 30 resolved hp.v2 names, against 0 under hp.v1. approach_notes stop citing an unobservable deciding line as the reason to stop. Brier skill against a coin on hp.v2 rises above the control's on the paired names.
ops.revert_if: Three outcomes would show this was wrong. First, over at least 30 resolved hp.v2 names, the paired Brier against the control is worse (mean difference above +0.01 with t above 1), or hp.v2's Brier skill against a coin falls below 0. Second, the drift alarm fires. Third, once 10 or more recommendations have resolved, fewer than half are right.

past_changes_review.evidence: The priced-in-as-claim part worked as intended: P4 is the most-cited helpful section in approach_notes and kept researchers from shorting visible misses (QBTS, HSAI, RSKD). The over-pessimism did not go away: 0 recommendations in 47 views, p_up confined to 38-58, and Brier skill of 0.003. There are no later revisions to review.

diagnosis: hp.v2 has 36 resolved names over 3 run days (11-12, 11-13, 11-16), so the gate is open and there is no drift alarm. Brier is 0.2257 (skill 0.097), against 0.2502 for hp.v1. Direction is 25/35, with 1 recommendation (a short, right, +3.3%). The version did not beat the frozen control on the same names: 28 pairs, Brier difference -0.001 (t -0.07). It ran in a window where 24 of 35 names fell, so most of the step up from hp.v1 is a researcher-wide down lean meeting a down tape, not the edits. The edits did change the method. Researchers now take the run-in apart (P6) and estimate the hidden line from its inputs (P7), and approach_notes name both as the most useful steps on about ten names. What they did not change is the spread: only 5 of 36 views sit 10 or more points from 50 (14%, against the 20% predicted), and only 1 recommendation came where 3 were predicted. The hunts show where the evidence is lost. Eight researchers built a down lean from dated inputs: a ramp management had floated that did not arrive, a guide that needed a quarter twice the run rate, restructuring advisers and a filing moved to its deadline, bridge financing, a debt negotiation. Each then pulled back toward 50 because the stock had already fallen a lot, and in no case showed that the price held the outcome the release would add. Those names are STEM 46, XTNT 40, LNZA 43, RCAT 38, VERI 40, DUOT 43, TMS 52 and NXB 41. Seven of the eight fell on the window (-28.9, -32.6, -29.1, -27.5, -17.7, -11.8, -3.8; NXB +2.0). STEM cut its revenue, ARR and cash-flow guide, which was the flip its own researcher had named. Four researchers wrote that the playbook has no guidance here: P4 'cuts both ways' on a fallen price (RCAT, XTNT, DUOT), and STEM asked for a note on equity that trades as an option on its debt. The same move happened upward on LFTO. A peer-driven run-up 'cancelled the beat lean', the release beat, and the stock rose 26.9%. A second damper sits in P9. It lets the self-critique move p_up only toward 50, so STEM, LNZA and LFTO each wrote that their own case was stronger than their number and left the number where it was. The return figures are correlated and are not used as evidence of direction: the eight names exited on two mornings in a weak small-cap tape, the hp.v1 name CURI shows a fall that really did hold the bad news (+15.2%), and NXB rose. The proposal rests on the reasoning gap the researchers reported themselves, not on these returns. It closes the loophole in P4's 'a price move you can tie to it' and makes P9 symmetric. It adds nothing, and it leaves P6 and P7 as they are, because both are doing what they were meant to do.

ops.title: "Priced in" is a claim to prove
ops.text:
The habit to break, measured on this repo's own stages: concluding the market holds a fact because it appeared in the news or in a downgrade. Awareness is not a number. Treat something as priced only when you can show it: a consensus that already reflects it, estimate revisions after the datapoint, a preview that quantifies it, or a price move you can tie to it. When you cannot show it, the gap between your answer and the stale number is unpriced.

A price move proves only what it can be tied to. A fall that came with dated news (a financing, a listing notice, a strategic review, a covenant waiver, last quarter's cut) holds that news. It does not hold the next step, which only this release can take: a further guide cut or a withdrawal, going-concern or impairment language, a raise or recapitalisation, or a ramp the company floated that did not arrive. The same holds upward: a run-up that came with peers' prints holds the peers, not this company's beat or raise. So a deep drawdown, a low multiple, a washed-out chart or a large run-in is not, by itself, a reason to pull p_up toward 50. Name the outcome the move is tied to, and ask whether your inputs point beyond it. If they do, the move is the bar and not the answer. Where the equity is small against debt or cash burn, a bad step in the release can change what the shares are worth outright, so a past fall does not cushion it.

Biases that keep a price behind: stale estimates (count the days since revision); anchoring on the company's guide after independent data moved; slow series the market underweights; thin coverage; extrapolating the last reaction; a consensus mean distorted by one outlier; crowded positioning that makes a small surprise move the stock a lot.

Be as willing to find a missed upside as a missed downside.
ops.rationale: P4 lists 'a price move you can tie to it' as proof that something is priced, and researchers have been using it loosely. A large fall that came with known stress was read as holding the release's own next step, so leans built from dated inputs were given back with no showing. Eight hp.v2 hunts did this (STEM, XTNT, LNZA, RCAT, VERI, DUOT, TMS, NXB). LFTO did the same upward on a peer-driven run-up. Four researchers wrote in approach_notes that P4 'cuts both ways' or that the playbook says nothing for a fallen price, and STEM asked for exactly this note. The edit keeps every existing sentence. It adds only the rule that ties a move to the outcome it can prove, which applies in both directions, and the mechanism for small equity under debt. It does not tell researchers to short fallen stocks. CURI (hp.v1), where a fall did hold the bad news, would be judged the same way, because there the move could be tied to the outcome.
ops.predicted_effect: Three effects, each measurable. (1) In hp.v3 hunts whose 20-day run-up is -15% or worse, or +15% or better, the mean |p_up-50| is no smaller than on the other names (under hp.v2 it was smaller, because those names were pulled to 50). (2) approach_notes stop saying that P4 'cuts both ways' on a fallen or run-up price; this was said in 4 hp.v2 hunts. (3) Together with the P9 edit, the share of views with |p_up-50| of 10 or more reaches at least 20% over the first 30 resolved hp.v3 names, with no worse paired Brier than the control.
ops.revert_if: Over at least 30 resolved hp.v3 names, revert if either of two things happens. (a) On names with a 20-day run-up of 15% or more in either direction, hp.v3's paired Brier against the control is worse by more than +0.01. (b) Views 10 or more points from 50 on such names are right on fewer than 55% of at least 10 cases. Either result would mean the fall or run-up really did hold the outcome more often than the researchers' inputs said.

ops.title: Before you emit
ops.text: Write the strongest case against your view and what in the release would flip it. Then read your number against what you wrote. If the case against is strong, move `p_up` toward 50 once. If writing it shows the opposite, that your own side's evidence is stronger than your number says, move `p_up` away from 50 by as much, once. Do either one there and nowhere else, and never emit a number your own critique says is wrong. In `approach_notes`, say in a line or two which parts of this playbook helped on this name and which got in the way: the stage reads those notes when it revises its approach.
ops.rationale: P9 is the last calibration step, and it can only shrink a view. When the critique finds the view too timid, the playbook has no move for it. Three hp.v2 researchers wrote that their own case was stronger than their number and then left the number unchanged: STEM ('the case for the downside is stronger than 46 implies', stayed 46, -28.9%), LNZA ('argues for a stronger down lean than 43', stayed 43, -29.1%), and LFTO ('the case for up is stronger than 56', stayed 56, +26.9%). The fourth, TMS, wrote that a reaffirmation was 'more likely than I allow', and the stock fell 3.8%. That case is included because a symmetric step will sometimes move the wrong way, and the revert condition below is built to catch it. Read together with the leaning views, hp.v2's 20 views 5 or more points from 50 were right 15 times against a stated confidence near 57%. That says the shrink-only step leaves the views under-confident, though the down tape inflates the count. The edit keeps the once-only rule and changes only its direction.
ops.predicted_effect: No hp.v3 hunt carries a self_critique that says the view is understated while p_up stays where it was (3 of 36 hp.v2 hunts did). The mean |p_up-50| rises from about 5.5 under hp.v2. Calibration holds: views 10 or more points from 50 are right at a rate at least equal to their mean stated confidence, and the paired Brier against the control is no worse.
ops.revert_if: Over at least 30 resolved hp.v3 names, revert if either of two things happens. (a) The paired Brier against the control is worse by more than +0.01 with t above 1. (b) Among views that the self-critique moved away from 50 (shown by the self_critique wording), fewer than half are right once 8 or more have resolved.

diagnosis: hp.v3 has 38 resolved names over 4 run days (11-18, 11-19, 11-20, 11-23). The gate is open and there is no drift alarm (60 recent pairs, diff +0.006, t 1.0). Brier is 0.2397 (skill 0.041) and direction 20/37, with 0 recommendations. Against the frozen control on the same 38 names the paired Brier difference is +0.001 (t 0.09), and the whole lineage against the control is -0.001 over 94 pairs (t -0.3). Three versions in, self-revision has not beaten the frozen approach. The two revisions aimed at widening p_up did not widen it: under hp.v3, 3 of 38 views (8%) sit 10 or more points from 50, against 14% under hp.v2 and a predicted 20%. Mean |p_up-50| is 5.0, against 4.4 for the control on the same names. This window was not a one-sided tape (19 names up, 19 down). The calibration data, pooled over every arm and version, are the strongest signal the stage has, and no revision has used them directly. Views 7 or more points from 50 were right 40 of 51 times (78%) while stating about 60. Under hp.v3 alone the figure is 8 of 9. Views 5-6 points out were right 39 of 70 (56%), and views within 5 points 41 of 95 (43%). So the information sits in the leans the researchers commit to, and those leans are understated, while the soft 53-56 band is a coin. The hunts show how the leans get shaded. Self-critiques set a case for each side beside the other and call it a tie: 'these roughly cancel', 'neither outweighs the other', 'each case carries similar weight, so 50 stands', 'neither side clears 65'. That happens on at least 7 of 38 (ANF, SMTC, HPE, DY, FUTU, RERE, TUYA). Two of those (FUTU, RERE) wrote that the case for up was stronger than their own number and still left the number unchanged. hp.v3's P9 edit was meant to stop exactly that, and both stocks rose. The tape-driven run-in split (P6) is the most-cited helpful step, on about 25 hunts, and is kept. The large misses (three AI-hardware names that fell on the print, two retail names that rose) clustered on one day and one tape, so they are not used as evidence of direction. The proposal makes two edits, both to calibration and none to what to search. P7 now tells the researcher what the stage's own record says about its leans: commit to a lean that has named evidence, and say 50 where there is none. P9 stops a two-sided critique from being read as a tie.

ops.title: Calibration and when to recommend
ops.text:
`p_up` is your honest probability that the stock is higher at the end of the window. 50 means you judge the two outcomes equally likely. Move away from 50 as far as the evidence takes you, and no less.

The line a print turns on (the next-period guide, the margin, bookings) is almost never visible before the release. That is the normal case and not, by itself, a reason to stay at 50. What you can see are its inputs: the company's record of guiding against what it then reported, counterparties' and peers' disclosures since it last spoke, your own arithmetic of what the line needs, and what consensus and the price assume about it. Estimate which way the line is likely to land against what the price holds, and let that estimate set p_up. Not being able to see the line is not the same as having shown that the price holds it (P8).

Read your own lean the way this stage's resolved record reads it. Across every arm, views that leaned 7 or more points from 50 have been right about three times in four while stating about 60. Views 5 or 6 points out have been a little better than a coin, and views within 5 points no better than one. So the information is in a lean you commit to, and it has been understated. If, after the search, you can name dated evidence that tilts the deciding line one way against what the price holds, give that lean its full size. Do not shade it back toward 50 because the line itself is unseen or because the recommendation bar below is not reached: those are why it is a lean and not a recommendation, and they are not reasons to shrink it. If you cannot name such evidence, write 50, not 53 or 47. A small tilt with nothing named behind it costs the score and says nothing.

Recommend (`action` long or short) only when all three hold:
- your probability that the direction is right is 65 or more;
- you can name the mechanism: the dated evidence that makes one side of the deciding line more likely than the price assumes, the reason the price does not hold it, and why this release will show it inside the window;
- your strongest case against it (`self_critique`) does not change your mind.

There is no quota. Zero recommendations on a day is fine; so are several.
ops.rationale: Two revisions have tried to widen p_up by removing reasons to shade (P7 in hp.v2, P4 and P9 in hp.v3), and the spread has not moved (14%, then 8%, of views 10 or more from 50). The researchers keep shading because nothing tells them their leans are understated. The record does say so, and it rests on far more than one week's returns. Over 51 views 7 or more from 50, pooled across the control and every evolving version, 78% were right at a stated confidence near 60 (hp.v3: 8 of 9, in a window with 19 names up and 19 down). The soft band is a coin: 56% at 5-6 points, 43% within 5. The edit keeps every sentence of the old P7 and the 65 bar, and adds the stage's own calibration as a fact for the researcher to use. That pushes views two ways: a named lean is stated fully, and an unnamed tilt goes to 50. It does not say which side to lean. Counter-cases in the evidence: HPE, SMTC and DY leaned 55-56 and fell. They sit in the 5-6 band the paragraph calls barely better than a coin, so the edit asks those researchers either to name what tilts the line or to write 50. It does not tell them to push further.
ops.predicted_effect: Over the first 30 resolved hp.v4 names: (1) the share of views 7 or more points from 50 rises from 24% (9/38 under hp.v3) to at least 35%; (2) the share in the soft band (|p_up-50| from 1 to 6) falls from about 74% to at most 50%, with more views at exactly 50; (3) views 7 or more from 50 stay right at least 65% of the time; (4) the paired Brier against the control is no worse than +0.005 and the Brier skill against a coin rises above the control's on the same names.
ops.revert_if: Over at least 30 resolved hp.v4 names, revert if either (a) views 7 or more points from 50 are right on fewer than 60% of at least 12 such views, which would mean the record's under-confidence was an artefact the researchers cannot exploit, or (b) the paired Brier against the control is worse by more than +0.01 with t above 1.

ops.title: Before you emit
ops.text: Write the strongest case against your view and what in the release would flip it. Then weigh it against your own case; do not set the two side by side and call it a tie. Before every print both directions have a story, so 'both cases are real' is not a finding and does not by itself mean 50. 50 says the two outcomes are equally likely, and it needs as much showing as any other number: say which evidence on each side is dated and tied to the deciding line, and which is a story that would fit any quarter. If the case against is stronger than you allowed, move `p_up` toward 50 once. If writing it shows your own side is stronger than your number says, move `p_up` away from 50 by as much, once. Do either one there and nowhere else. If your critique says one side is stronger than your number, the number changes: never emit a number your own critique calls wrong. In `approach_notes`, say in a line or two which parts of this playbook helped on this name and which got in the way: the stage reads those notes when it revises its approach.
ops.rationale: hp.v3 made the P9 step symmetric, and its prediction failed in the very way it was meant to prevent. FUTU and RERE each wrote that the case for up was stronger than their number, and each kept the number. Both stocks rose. The researchers did not read P9 as 'test my view against its strongest rival'. They read it as 'write the case for each side and see whether they cancel'. At least 7 of 38 hp.v3 self-critiques end that way ('these roughly cancel', 'neither outweighs the other', 'each case carries similar weight, so 50 stands': ANF, SMTC, HPE, DY, FUTU, RERE, TUYA). Two plausible stories always exist around a 10% event, so this template pulls views to 50 whatever the evidence weighs, and that matches the coin-like soft band in the calibration data. The edit keeps the once-only symmetric step. It adds that a tie must be shown rather than assumed, and that a critique which calls the number wrong must change it. It names no side. ANF, SMTC and TUYA are cited as instances of the template, not as cases where weighing would have known the answer.
ops.predicted_effect: In hp.v4 hunts: (1) no self_critique says one side is stronger than the emitted number while the number stays where it was (2 of 38 under hp.v3, 3 of 36 under hp.v2); (2) self_critiques that conclude 'the cases cancel, so near 50' fall from at least 7 of 38 to at most 3 of 30, and a view emitted at 50 states why the two outcomes are equally likely; (3) at least 3 hunts per 30 record a move away from 50 made by the critique (0 under hp.v3).
ops.revert_if: Over at least 30 resolved hp.v4 names, revert if either (a) the views the self-critique moved away from 50 (shown by the self_critique wording) are right fewer than half the time once 8 or more have resolved, or (b) the paired Brier against the control is worse by more than +0.01 with t above 1.
